sections.heading: Roof Cleaning and Moss Removal, Defined

c.v: Roof cleaning and moss removal in Newark, NJ

runs.v: clears biological growth — moss, Gloeocapsa magma algae, and lichen — from residential and commercial roofs with a low-pressure chemical wash that kills the growth at the root without damaging asphalt shingles. For homeowners, landlords, property managers, and commercial building owners in Newark and Essex County, this matters when dark streaks, green patches, or lifting growth start shortening roof life, trapping moisture, and raising the risk of leaks and costly repairs.

Newark Quality Roofing provides professional roof cleaning and moss removal services in Newark, NJ, using specialized equipment and low-pressure methods that follow ARMA specifications instead of pressure washing, which can strip protective granules. In this guide, you’ll find how roof cleaning and moss removal works, the signs a roof needs cleaning, the step-by-step process, prevention treatments, residential and commercial service options, costs and estimates, and why professional cleaning helps restore curb appeal, improve air quality, and extend the roof’s lifespan.

sections.heading: Roof Cleaning and Moss Removal We Provide in Newark, NJ

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing is one of the roof cleaning companies that specialize in roof cleaning services for Newark and Essex County residential and commercial properties, with additional coverage in Morris County.

runs.v: Roof cleaning removes dirt and grime as well as moss, Gloeocapsa magma algae, and lichen to keep a clean roof, using a chemical wash at low pressure to kill growth at the root and rinse the dead material away without stripping the protective granules. Removing dirt, algae, and grime can also help the roof reflect heat more effectively.

A Newark Quality Roofing roof cleaning uses a low-pressure chemical method, because the Asphalt Roofing Manufacturers Association (ARMA) states that pressure-washing an asphalt shingle roof causes granule loss and premature failure of the roof system. ARMA specifies a 50:50 mix of laundry-strength liquid chlorine bleach and water, a 15–20-minute dwell, and a low-pressure rinse, so a Newark Quality Roofing wash relies on chemical action rather than mechanical force across Essex County. That low-pressure approach is part of professional roof cleaning services designed to protect asphalt shingle roofs.

c.v: Moss removal

items.v: — Moss removal is designed to remove moss from shingle edges, valleys, and shaded north-facing slopes, because ARMA states that moss lifts and curls the leading edges of shingles and raises the risk of shingle blow-off during wind events.

c.v: Algae streak removal

items.v: — Algae streak removal clears unsightly black streaks and black algae streaks caused by Gloeocapsa magma, the most prevalent roof-discoloration algae, which feeds on the limestone filler in asphalt shingles, per ARMA and Atlas Roofing.

c.v: Lichen removal

items.v: — Lichen removal clears the crusty grey-green patches that adhere to shaded shingle surfaces, applying the ARMA 50:50 chlorine-bleach-and-water solution at a 15–20-minute dwell to penetrate the growth to the root.

c.v: Soft-wash low-pressure roof cleaning

items.v: — Soft-wash low-pressure roof cleaning applies the cleaning solution and a low-pressure rinse rather than a pressure washer, because ARMA states that pressure-washing an asphalt shingle roof causes granule loss and premature failure of the roof system.

c.v: Algae and moss prevention treatment

items.v: — Algae and moss prevention treatment slows regrowth after a cleaning, because proper maintenance extends asphalt-shingle service life by roughly 25–30%, per ARMA, and some roofs need prevention sooner due to environmental factors like shade and nearby trees, with the prevention-treatment cost range named in the cost section, per This Old House.

c.v: Commercial low-slope roof cleaning

items.v: — Commercial low-slope roof cleaning matches the chemistry and rinse to EPDM, TPO, and modified-bitumen membranes, managing drainage during the rinse so cleaning solution does not pond on the low-slope membrane.

sections.heading: How Our Roofing Contractors Perform Roof Cleaning and Moss Removal

runs.v: Low-Pressure Chemical Wash to ARMA Specification

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing contractors clean a roof with low pressure washing on appropriate roof surfaces and a low-pressure chemical wash, not a pressure washer, because ARMA states that pressure-washing an asphalt shingle roof causes granule loss and premature failure of the roof system.

runs.v: Trained crews also use specialized equipment for safety during roof work. A Newark Quality Roofing wash applies the ARMA 50:50 mix of laundry-strength liquid chlorine bleach and water, holds the solution on the surface for the 15–20-minute dwell ARMA specifies, and finishes with a low-pressure rinse, so the cleaning relies on chemical action that kills moss, Gloeocapsa magma algae, and lichen at the root. Heavy moss is removed by hand before the wash, because moss lifts and curls the shingle leading edges, per ARMA.
Prevention and Algae-Resistant Measures

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing recommends preventive measures after a cleaning, because proper maintenance extends asphalt-shingle service life by roughly 25–30%, per ARMA.

runs.v: Preventing moss growth can also require trimming overhanging branches that keep shaded slopes damp. Zinc and copper metal molecules inhibit algae growth, per ARMA and Atlas Roofing, so manufacturers build copper granules into algae-resistant shingles. ARMA states that adding zinc or copper strips to an existing roof is not recommended, because the strips require exposed nails that cause leaks over time or break the sealant bond, so Newark Quality Roofing reserves strip installation for a roof replacement and prevents regrowth on an existing roof with a maintenance wash.

sections.heading: Commercial Roof Cleaning and Moss Removal We Provide

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing cleans commercial low-slope roofs across Essex County, matching the cleaning chemistry and rinse to EPDM rubber, TPO, and modified-bitumen membranes and managing drainage so cleaning solution does not pond on the membrane.

runs.v: EPDM lasts 15–25 years, TPO 7–20 years, and modified bitumen 20 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, and biological growth that holds moisture against the membrane accelerates the deterioration.

Ponding water remaining on a low-slope roof more than 48 hours counts as a defect, and a flat roof needs at least ¼ inch per foot of slope to drain, per the NRCA and ARMA, so a Newark Quality Roofing crew clears the drains during the rinse. A Newark Quality Roofing commercial cleaning pairs with an inspection that follows the NRCA cadence of twice per year, spring and fall, plus an inspection after any major weather event.
